title: The 5 Hottest Planets, Ranked (the Closest to the Sun Is Only #2)

scenes.text: The planet closest to the Sun is not the hottest. Not even close.

scenes.label: Jupiter · -110°C
scenes.text: Number five: Jupiter. About minus one hundred ten degrees Celsius, measured where its air is as thick as ours.

scenes.label: Mars · -65°C
scenes.text: Number four: Mars. Around minus sixty-five degrees Celsius, a frozen red desert.

scenes.label: Earth · 15°C
scenes.text: Number three: Earth. An average of fifteen degrees Celsius, warm enough for liquid water.

scenes.label: Mercury · 167°C
scenes.text: Number two: Mercury. Only one hundred sixty-seven degrees on average, swinging from four hundred thirty by day to minus one eighty at night.

scenes.label: Venus · 464°C
scenes.text: Number one: Venus. Four hundred sixty-four degrees Celsius, hot enough to melt lead. Thick air traps the heat.

description:
The five hottest planets in our solar system, ranked by average temperature.
Mercury is closest to the Sun, but Venus is hotter because its thick atmosphere traps heat.
Which planet would you visit first?
first_comment: Would you rather stand on Venus or Mercury? And what should we rank next?
